critical_code_review_comments: StorySectionsEditor.jsx legacy-block id backfill is correct: uses React.useMemo with a stable dependency derived from (length + joined ids) AND a one-shot useEffect that calls onChange?.(safeBlocks) only when at least one block lacks an id. This is the right pattern to avoid input focus loss on legacy data — confirmed empirically: typing in ss-text-1 keeps document.activeElement === ss-text-1.
ProjectGalleryEditor.jsx applies the same backfill pattern for gallery items — also confirmed visually (Villa Travertino legacy 'Living room' rendered as pg-card-0 without flicker).

Both editors use Math.random() in the legacy-id fallback. If the parent re-renders with a different array reference but same content, useMemo dependency `blocks.length + joined ids` masks it, but a more robust approach would be a content hash or `legacy_${i}` only (idempotent across renders). Current implementation works but is one re-render-trick away from regressing.
Editorial Studio route silently logs the user out on backend 5xx — UX antipattern. A 5xx on a secondary fetch should surface as an error toast, not destroy the session.
StorySectionsEditor uses native confirm() for delete (line 80) — disruptive UX, prefer a sonner confirm or inline two-step. Mentioned for design polish, not a blocker.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of Editorial Studio failure: a chain of 503s from the editorial page mount (suspected /api/markets/editions which has been failing since iteration_64) is interpreted by the SPA's global error handler as an auth failure, clearing the access token cookie and redirecting to /auth/login. This is a TWO-layer fix: (a) repair the upstream 500 on /api/markets/editions for the demo tenant, (b) make the SPA's fetch interceptor treat 5xx differently from 401 — do NOT log out on 5xx, surface an error banner instead. The same cascade then knocks subsequent navigations (CRM accounts, public project page) onto /auth/login because cookies are already cleared. Reproduction: login → navigate to /blueprint/projects-studio (works) → navigate to /blueprint/editorial (URL becomes /auth/login within 3.5s). Workaround for QA: test routes independently from a fresh login each time.
